claims.text: The as-cast CoCrFeNiMn alloy is chemically homogeneous.
The as-cast CoCrFeNiMn alloy is single-phase and polycrystalline.
Low-temperature aging at a selected temperature and time will nucleate nanoscale precipitates in CoCrFeNiMn.
The aging-induced nanoscale precipitates will be uniformly distributed within the matrix.
The thermal aging treatment will modify microstructure without changing the alloy's overall composition.
The nanoscale precipitates will act as magnetic domain-wall pinning centers.
Pinning by the precipitates will hinder magnetic domain-wall motion.
Hindered domain-wall motion will increase the field required for reversal and therefore increase coercivity.
The aged CoCrFeNiMn sample will have a higher room-temperature coercive field than the matched as-cast sample.
The coercivity increase should hold when aging forms nanoscale precipitates without significant grain coarsening or detrimental phase transformations.
The magnitude of the coercivity change will depend on aging temperature and time.
The magnitude of the coercivity change will depend on precipitate size and distribution.
Room-temperature hysteresis measurements should use matched field-sweep conditions so that aging is the controlled variable.
A lack of a statistically significant coercivity increase in the aged sample would falsify the predicted outcome.
Failure to observe nanoscale precipitates by TEM after aging would falsify the proposed intervention-to-mediator link.
